chapter_theme: The distinctions of Shakti (சத்தி பேதம்): the Goddess Tripura, under many names (Tripurasundari, Manonmani, Parashakti, Abhirami, Bhuvanapati, Varahi, Omkari), is the source of the worlds, the tattvas, nada and bindu, speech and mantra, never apart from Siva; worshipped, she enters the poet's heart, clears his deluded mind and shows him the way to Siva.
structure_note: Each verse begins with the last word of the one before (அந்தாதி). Verses on her cosmic nature (1045 to 1048, 1052 to 1056, 1059, 1065, 1070, 1074) alternate with iconographic portraits (1049 to 1051, 1067, 1072, 1073) and with the poet's own experience of her entering him (1058, 1060, 1061, 1064, 1066). Despite the title, the verses do not describe the diagram of the Tripura chakra itself.

1045.reading: Mahamaya, maya, the bindu-born, the spoken word, the Om-maya and the inner light, and the mantras that are herself among the six crores, are the forms of Shakti; being and not being, there is Tripura.
1045.nuance: வயிந்தவம் (baindava, born of bindu) and வைகரி (vaikhari, speech at its spoken level) are terms of Saiva cosmology and mantra theory; ஓமாயை and ஓராறு கோடி (six crores, taken of the mantras) are obscure. ஆமாய் அலவாம் can be read 'she is and is not' or 'she is all and none of these'.

1046.reading: Tripura, Sundari, Antari, the vermilion one, Paripurai, Narani, the one of many colours, Isi who removes darkness, Manonmani: by these names the great one stands as many.
1046.nuance: A string of the Goddess's names; several (அந்தரி, of the sky; நாரணி, the female Narayana; மனோன்மனி, she who lifts the mind beyond mind) carry traditional meanings, others (பரிபுரை) are unclear. மாமது in the last line is obscure: 'the great one' or 'great honey'.

1047.reading: In the three cities she formed herself, three forms of one nature, she who is gold, red and white is learning, and she herself grants enjoyment and release.
1047.nuance: The three colours are traditionally matched with three goddesses (gold with Lakshmi, red with Durga or Shakti, white with Sarasvati) who are one Tripura; the verse only says three forms are one. Granting both போகம் and முத்தி, worldly enjoyment and release, is the claim Srividya makes for this goddess.

1048.reading: Tripura grants nada and nada's end; the supreme bindu, which multiplies, becomes the earth and the worlds; Parai, Abhirami, she who is beyond the senses, embraces, gives grace, gives that wisdom and rules.
1048.nuance: நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) and பரவிந்து (supreme bindu) are stages of manifestation in Saiva cosmology. அகோசரி is 'she who is not an object of the senses'. போதம் is taken as wisdom; the last line is compressed.

1049.reading: Anklets on her feet, red silk her garment, breasts bound with a band, the sugarcane bow and flower arrows, the goad and the noose, a fine crown, and earrings of dark great gems: such is she.
1049.nuance: A portrait of Tripurasundari with her standard emblems. Tradition reads the noose as desire or attachment, the goad as restraint, the sugarcane bow as the mind and the five flower arrows as the senses; the verse gives the emblems without their meanings.

1050.reading: She with earrings, with brows like a killing bow, with a form of lasting blood-red colour, with beads and necklace, rayed crown and the great moon, Chandika stands holding up the four directions.
1050.nuance: The gentle portrait of 1049 turns fierce here: கொலைவில் (killing bow) and சண்டிகை (Chandika, the fierce goddess) show the same goddess in her terrible aspect. கண்டிகை is usually a bead string, often rudraksha.

1051.reading: Tripura who stands, the ancient one who extends, the undiminishing Mohini, the one of the crest, who knows the good, who wears beads, Karidani of four limbs, the pure one of the pure lotus.
1051.nuance: Another list of names. மாதிருக்கும் சிகை and நாற்கால் கரீடணி are obscure; the second may be a corrupt form of a Sanskrit name. Only புராதனி (the ancient), மோகினி (the enchantress) and சுத்தை (the pure) are clear.

1052.reading: She is the tattvas, the heavy-breasted, the rising of bliss; as the substance she rules, the great Shakti, the great Parai; all those things, and the smaller than the atom, she is, and she is the mind of the form she set up.
1052.nuance: பாரத தனத்தி is taken as பார தனத்தி (of heavy breasts); சுகோதயள் is 'rising of bliss' and வத்துவம் is vastu, substance or reality. அணோரணி echoes the Upanishadic 'smaller than the small'. The last line (கோல மதியவள்) can also mean she is the moon of that form.

1053.reading: There are no gods who do not know her, no rare austerity done without her, nothing the five can achieve without her, and without her I know no way of entering the city.
1053.nuance: The plainest verse of the chapter, built on the repeated அவளன்றி (without her). ஐவர் (the five) are traditionally the five gods who perform the five acts, but may be the five senses; ஊர் (the town) is traditionally the city of release or Siva's realm.

1054.reading: The knowers say Parashakti is bliss; they say she is both formless and with form; they say action is her will; and the knowers say the Supreme too is in her.
1054.nuance: The verse reports what knowers (அறிவார்) say rather than asserting it in the poet's voice. பரனும் அவளிடத்தான் can mean the Supreme is within her or is on her side, as in the half-woman form; either way Siva and Shakti are not apart.

1055.reading: Wherever he is, there is the lady Mahadevi; wherever there is flesh, he is there as the breath of the life within; wherever the sky is, he is there and beyond it: see the many signs of the king who stands everywhere.
1055.nuance: உள்ளுயிர்க் காலவன் is taken as கால் (wind, breath) of the inner life; it could also be read with காலம் (time). The verse moves from his inseparability from the Goddess to his presence in bodies and beyond the sky.

1056.reading: You do not grasp how Parashakti, Mahashakti, stands in many ways as the power of the earth, as the strong power through every age; Parashakti is the enjoyment that is merit.
1056.nuance: தராசத்தி (the earth's power) is fairly clear; உராசத்தி is obscure, taken as 'strong power' or 'the power in the breast'. The last line makes the Goddess herself the fruit of merit (புண்ணியம்) enjoyed.

1057.reading: Sharing half his body with the curl-haired Shakti who brings enjoyment, he stands there as Parashakti; taking a body there, she is the branch along which the knowledge that ripens devotees spreads each day.
1057.nuance: பாகஞ்செய்து is read first as sharing a half (the half-woman form) and then, in பாகஞ்செய் ஞானம், as ripening; the pun is the verse's hinge. கொம்பு (branch, creeper's support) prepares the next verse's கொம்பனையாள. Who is subject of the first two lines, Siva or Shakti, is not fixed.

1058.reading: Trusting, I desired and placed within me the one like a creeper, the maiden of full breasts with a fragrant opening garland, the one of the channel shining to the sky, the little girl whose holy body is red coral.
1058.nuance: The love lyric's vocabulary turned on the Goddess. வானவிர் நாடி is taken as the nadi that shines up to the sky, traditionally the central channel; a plain reading is less clear. நம்பி may be 'trusting' or an address to a man ('O Nambi').

1059.reading: The things set in place, the many lives that join bodies, the ten faces, Parai and Paraparai, the workings of the mind and its instruments, and the Shakti who makes them act: of all these she is the head of knowledge.
1059.nuance: பத்து முகம் (ten faces) may be the ten directions or ten forms of the Goddess. வித்தைத் தலையவள் is read as the head of vidya (knowledge), and is a name in Srividya; it may also be the head of all the listed things.

1060.reading: The leader, the lady of broad breasts, the peacock of the pure path who does unending austerity, the maiden who conquers many arts, has filled my heart and stands here so that it is steady.
1060.nuance: தொலைவில் தவம் is read as தொலைவு இல், austerity without end; it could also be austerity done far off. The Goddess as one who herself does tapas is a well-known image (Parvati's penance for Siva). The verse's point is the last line: her filling the heart makes it stable.

1061.reading: She who stood, the finely jewelled one, joined with the long kala, settled into my inner self while the seven worlds worship her; at one with the hall, Manonmani the auspicious became one with me and, matching me, closed it.
1061.nuance: நீள்கலை (the long kala) is technical and unclear. மன்று (the hall) may be the hall of Siva's dance at Tillai or its inner counterpart. ஒத்து அடைத்தாள் ('matching, she closed') may mean she shut the doors of the senses or closed the way of return; the verse does not say.

1062.reading: People do not discern how Manonmani, the auspicious, the jewelled one in the lotus where all subsides alike, who does all this as the great Lord, closes off the mind that churns.
1062.nuance: The word order is compressed and the reading is tentative. மத்து (churning stick) is taken of the agitated mind; சித்தடைக்கும் வழி is read as the way she stops the mind (சித்தம்), in keeping with மனோன்மனி, she who lifts beyond mind.

1063.reading: Knowing, she stands at once as the inner light; when the lady of fragrant flower-hair and he stand joined, she grants the goal to those who rise, ripened.
1063.nuance: கணிந்தெழுவார் is taken as கனிந்து எழுவார், those who rise ripened; it could also be 'those who reckon and rise'. The union of Siva and Shakti is the condition of grace in this reading.

1064.reading: The girl gentle as grace, Ananda Sundari, looked at my inner self, like a mean fruit gone sour, made it clear, showed me the way to Siva, set me in light and took me into herself so that I would be saved.
1064.nuance: அளி is grace or the bee; 'bee-like girl' is also possible. The fruit image runs to the end: the sour fruit is made clear and sweet, and உண்டாள் (she ate) completes it, the soul consumed by the Goddess as its rescue.

1065.reading: What was called 'is' and 'is not' took form and stood, settled and filled the hall of rich Tillai; they have not seen it: with the cause and she who causes, she stands settled so the three spheres are joined.
1065.nuance: தில்லை மன்று is the hall at Chidambaram where Siva dances. காரண காரணி may be 'the cause and the causing one', Siva and Shakti. மண்டலம் முன்றுற is read as மூன்று, the three spheres traditionally of sun, moon and fire; the line is uncertain.

1066.reading: She stood as his body and life; Parashakti, who joins the way to Siva, went in and, entering me as one, became my awareness; the supreme light stood with her whose hand holds the leaf.
1066.nuance: சென்றான் and நின்றான் are masculine while the subject seems to be Shakti; the verse may move between the two as one. ஏடங்கையாள் is taken as 'she with the palm-leaf book in her hand', a Sarasvati attribute; ஏடு may also be a petal.

1067.reading: The lady with the leaf in her hand, our sovereign, the three-eyed one, whose guise is crystal, who loves the white lotus: wear Parvati's feet, sung in the holy hymns, on your head, and let your mouth speak her praise.
1067.nuance: Crystal, the white lotus and the book are Sarasvati's marks, given here to Parvati, so the verse makes the goddesses one. திருமுறை may mean the sacred hymns generally or the Saiva canon by name.

1068.reading: Praising and worshipping her paired feet so that they are gained, the way of worship is set; she who looks out with goad, noose and green sugarcane, the flower-child, is everything to the Primal One.
1068.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 repeat பார்த்திடும் and are obscure; பசுங்கரும்பு may be the green sugarcane bow of 1049. வழிபடு மாறிடும் may mean 'the way of worship' or 'worship changes (one)'.

1069.reading: Placing in the middle the name of the jewelled one on the flower, the younger sister of Mal who in many ways made the world, and practising it many times on the fingers, light grows and all three times appear.
1069.nuance: The Goddess as Vishnu's (மால்) sister is a common Saiva identification. The practice looks like repeating her name or mantra counted on the fingers, with knowledge of past, present and future (முக்காலம்) as its fruit; பாதியில் வைத்து (placing in the half or middle) and நீதி மலர் are unclear.

1070.reading: The gentle one who is the sixteen beginning with Medha, Paraparai who shines in the texts beginning with the Veda, she who is the support and spreads as the examined expanse, is the good grace of nada and what precedes nada.
1070.nuance: மேதாதி ஈரெட்டும் (sixteen beginning with Medha) is traditionally taken of sixteen kalas or powers; the list is not given. ஆதாரம் may be the bodily centres (ādhāras) as well as 'support'.

1071.reading: Come, you people, and hear it from those who have received grace: I praise the red feet, which hold the rare true thing, of Bhuvanapati, who turns the deluded mind into a mind that has found the true thing.
1071.nuance: The verse turns on பொருள (the true thing, meaning) and மருள் (delusion). Read this way, பொருள்பெற்ற சிந்தை describes the mind she gives, not her own; the line also allows 'Bhuvanapati of the mind that holds the truth'.

1072.reading: She of the boar's face and her station, with the pestle that pounds the base boar and holding the other weapon, the plough, the white-smiling one rises high in the hearts of those who know her without flaw.
1072.nuance: A portrait of Varahi, the boar-faced goddess, whose traditional weapons are the pestle and plough. ஈன வராகம் (the base boar) in line 2 is obscure; it may be a boar-demon or a corruption.

1073.reading: She is called Omkari, a girl of unfading green; becoming Ahankari she bore the five, and she sits sweetly within Hrinkara.
1073.nuance: ஓங்காரி (she who is Om), ஆங்காரி (she who is ahamkara, the sense of I) and ரீங்காரம் (the seed syllable hrim, sacred to the Goddess) play on one sound. ஐவர் may be the five gods or the five elements, which in Samkhya arise through ahamkara.

1074.reading: Tatparai, who stood as the leader herself, herself sowed lives and gave the fourteen worlds, the place of the gods, the mind and good intellect; she herself is also the nature of the way to Siva.
1074.nuance: The repeated தானே (she herself) gathers the chapter: creation, the inner faculties and the path to release are all hers. பதினாலும் is taken as the fourteen worlds, which the verse doesn't name.

links.note: Both name Mahamaya and speech among the first powers; in 1925 they shine within bindu, in 1045 they and the bindu-born (வயிந்தவம்) are all forms of one Tripura. The bindu chapter's cosmology here gets a goddess's face.

Both make the Goddess the one who unfolds as nada and bindu: 1048 has Tripura grant nada and nada's end while the supreme bindu becomes the worlds, 1138 has Sivashakti spread out as bindu and nada within the mind.
Both portraits give the Goddess the noose and goad. Tripura (1049) adds the sugarcane bow and flower arrows; Bhairavi (1081) adds the trident and skull. Same emblems, gentle and fierce forms.

1053 says no god fails to know her and nothing the five do is done without her; 1087 says the many gods, Siva, Brahma and Vishnu among them, look to the Lady as cause. Both put the Goddess behind every god.
1066 has her stand as his body and life; 1137 says the lady and he stand in one form and people do not see it. Both deny any gap between Siva and Shakti.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow at the feet of the Lord of eight qualities as useless as a sense that cannot sense; Tirumular tells the head to wear the Goddess's feet and the mouth to praise her. The same claim for the head, turned to the Goddess.

The Kural traces joyless birth to the delusion (மருள்) that takes what is not real as real (பொருள்). Tirumular uses the same pair: the Goddess turns the deluded mind into one that has found the true thing, so grace is the remedy for the Kural's diagnosis.

source_issues: 1063: line 1 reads நிறகும், a misprint for நிற்கும்.
1065: line 4 மண்டல முன்றுற is probably மூன்றுற (three); read so here.
1046 (மாமது), 1051 line 3 (நாற்கால் கரீடணி), 1056 (உராசத்தி), 1068 lines 3 and 4 and 1072 line 2 (ஈன வராகம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
